segment.description: Big Swan Creek (GNIS 01269345), a substantial Duck River tributary of south-central Tennessee draining from the Lewis County headwaters (Gordensburg area) southeast to its mouth on the Duck River in eastern Maury County. Identity resolved from the catalog's hydroIdentity (GNIS 01269345, HUC 06040003 Lower Duck): all 133 NHD flowline segments carry reachcodes 06040003xxxxxx, and WQP station metadata places stations in Lewis Co. (101) and Maury Co. (081). This is NOT the Swan Creek of Houston/Stewart counties (Cumberland basin) - that different water is excluded by the catalog HUC.
segment.boundaries: Catalog gives no reach limits; record covers the HUC 06040003 main stem from upper Lewis County (USGS 03601852 at Gordensburg, 38.7 sq mi, 620 ft datum) to the lower Maury County reaches (TDEC stations at Short Branch Rd and Raleigh Chapel Rd, ~35.71-35.75 N). Little Swan Creek (Lewis Co.) is a separate named tributary and its stations are excluded from the facts below.

coldSource.notes: Low-elevation Western Highland Rim stream: gauge datum 620 ft NGVD29 at the Gordensburg station. No tailwater or documented cold-water source. Searches surfaced only non-citable mentions (paddle-guide app, Fishbrain, Grokipedia) describing a narrow, shallow, moderate-gradient creek.

holdover.detail: No trout stockings exist to hold over: the live 2026 TWRA datatable (616 rows, fetched 2026-09-18) contains zero 'Swan' rows statewide, and the catalog carries stockingProgram: false. No agency holdover documentation exists.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documentation found; absent from TWRA wild trout, delayed-harvest, and special-regulation lists; only statewide trout rules apply.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: The only summer samples on record (USGS Gordensburg 2000, TDEC Short Branch Rd 2003-2004, TDEC Lewis Co. 2019-2023) run 19.5-23.1 C - warmwater summer conditions on an unstocked stream with no trout documentation.
